analysis: Examined both files, metadata, patches and supplied surrounding documentation. docs/architecture/inference.md head lines 253–260 newly describe complete SSD checkpoint imports occurring off the engine queue, concurrently with another request's prefill, using host-backed destinations without evaluation or fencing. changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md lines 3–9 reports lower staging latency and an opt-in real-model contention regression. These documentation changes alone do not establish a concrete security regression. Relevant contracts are A-001, TB-007, T-028 and T-041: plaintext checkpoint ownership, safe concurrent device access, authenticated account-scoped reuse and bounded staging reservations. Faster hit latency is not independently a new timing-oracle class; T-041 already accepts the narrower same-account oracle. Surrounding baseline docs describe pre-submit deadline checks/reservations (lines 244–251), receipt-bound cache evidence and actual billing counts (253–258), and device-transfer activity accounting (390–398). Integration must inspect CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift and the referenced destination contract in docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md, neither supplied, plus bridge/cache callers and tests: verify host-copy completion and lifetime before adoption, no shared mutable aliases, authentication/type/layout validation before exposure, cancellation/error cleanup, staging-memory charges and unbounded-activity receipts during concurrent prefill. No supplied change alters authorization, attestation, hop encryption, disk crypto, cache scope, TTL or billing policy. Missing implementation and test evidence prevents validating the new synchronization claim; this is a coverage limit, not proof of safety or a finding.
